The header has no bottom border or divider while the outer article retains the existing rounded semantic card surface, light border, and shadow

resolvedDecisions.question: How should the requirement that the shipment menu is always visible apply to received, cancelled, and unassigned shipment groups, for which the current UI intentionally exposes no shipment actions?
options: Always show an enabled menu and define which non-mutating or newly available actions it contains for those states
Always show the trigger but disable it when the shipment has no valid actions, preserving current business permissions
Keep hiding the trigger when no valid actions exist, treating always visible as applying only to actionable active shipments
resolvedDecisions.recommendation: Always render the trigger in the same aligned slot but disable it for received, cancelled, and unassigned groups. This meets the visual consistency goal without inventing actions or changing the current active-state permissions.
resolvedDecisions.answer: Always show the trigger and disable it when the shipment has no valid actions.

resolvedDecisions.question: Should the initial visible-book limit stay at the current three books or become four so the desktop two-column grid starts with complete rows?
options: Keep the existing three-book limit and preserve the exact current expansion threshold
Use four books initially so desktop starts with two complete rows while preserving the Show N more books action
resolvedDecisions.recommendation: Use four. It is a presentation-only change that matches the new two-column composition and keeps the required expansion action and all data unchanged.
resolvedDecisions.answer: Use an initial visible-book limit of four.
resolvedDecisions.specRef: Books: two columns; Show N more books

resolvedDecisions.question: Should the delivery preview contract and backend mapper expose series totalBooks so the exact position label such as 1 з 6 can be rendered?
options: Expand the contract and backend mapper to include series totalBooks
Keep the no-API constraint and omit the total
resolvedDecisions.recommendation: Expand the contract because deriving the total from visible order books would be incorrect.
resolvedDecisions.answer: Expand the delivery preview contract and backend mapper with totalBooks.

verifiedAssertions.claim: The In transit page already renders DeliveryOrderCard from the delivery feature and supplies the existing order, shipment, book, selection, and receive callbacks.
The current card model already contains all display data required by the redesign, so no API or data-structure change is required.
Store name, order number/date metadata, and order status already render on the left side of the header.
Book count and total currently render as one combined string, not as a total-first hierarchy.
The current header has the divider that the redesign asks to remove.
Shipment details currently use a heavy rounded bordered nested section and label/value metadata blocks.
The existing shipment heading, status chip, tracking link, and active shipment actions can be reused.
Books currently render in a single vertical list with light dividers, a 40 px 3:4 cover, and no per-book rounded border.
The current book row already renders title, author, optional series/volume text, and price.
The Show N more books behavior already exists with an initial limit of three and expands across shipment groups without hiding later shipment metadata.
The order menu is already always visible, but shipment menus are currently hidden for inactive and unassigned groups.
Book menus are currently visible at all viewport sizes rather than hover/focus-revealed on desktop.
All three dropdown types already use content-sized, non-wrapping menu contents due to the current uncommitted nowrap change.
The existing shared semantic tokens and StatusBadge already provide cream/card surfaces, terracotta primary accents, soft info chips, heading serif typography, rounded corners, borders, and shadows.
